title: Symmetric Boundary
statement:
Symmetrical figures are beautiful-and they are the subject of this task. Aregion in a 2D plane isconvex
if, for every pair of points p and q in the region, the segment connectingp and q is entirely included in
the region. Also, a region in a 2D plane ispoint-symmetric if, when you rotate the region by 180 degrees
around a certain point, the rotated region exactly matches the original region.
You are given a convex polygon in a 2D plane with n vertices, number ed from 1 to n in counterclockwise
order. Vertex i has coordinates (xi, yi). No three vertices are collinear. Determine whether there exists
a convex, point-symmetric region containing all of then vertices on its boundary. If one or more such
regions exist, compute the minimum area among all of them.

input:
The first line of input contains one integer n (3 ≤ n ≤ 30). Each of the nextn lines contains two integers.
The i-th line contains xi and yi (0 ≤ xi, yi ≤ 1000).
It is guaranteed that the given polygon is convex, its vertices are given in counterclockwise order, and no
three of its vertices are collinear.
output:
If one or more such regions exist, output the minimum area among all of them. The relative error of the
output must be with in10−9.
If such a region does not exist, output-1 instead.
